 Keegan Murray (ankle) is available for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Sunday’s game will be Murray’s first since October 23. It’s unclear whether his playing time will be limited, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see Murray’s minutes go well into the thirties. Precious Achiuwa has been the starting power forward in Murray’s absence.

 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury.

 Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is available to play against the Lakers on Wednesday. 
 As expected, Achiuwa will be good to go against Los Angeles. He’ll continue to start in place of Keegan Murray, who is still sidelined with an ankle injury. Achiuwa has had a couple productive outings, but he isn’t the best streaming option on a 14-game day.

 Achiuwa, who has been starting for the injured Keegan Murray (ankle), played 27 minutes in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. The probable tag suggests he’ll be available, and Achiuwa should remain in the starting lineup if so. 
 Precious Achiuwa

 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa contributed 24 points (12-of-17 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists and four steals on Thursday against the Pelicans. 
 For the third straight game, Achiuwa got the starting nod in place of Keegan Murray (ankle), and this was his best performance of the season. He set a new season high for scoring and nearly finished with a double-double. Murray is set to be re-evaluated in early November, but Achiuwa should have at least a few more starts, making him worth considering as a streaming option with the Kings playing four games next week.

Precious Achiuwa moved into the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and three blocks in 39 minutes. He’s a worthwhile pickup while Murray sits, but fantasy managers will likely take a hit in free-throw percentage.

Achiuwa played 39 minutes against the Grizzlies and recorded a double-double with five “stocks.” Sacramento plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Spurs on Tuesday, and Achiuwa would be a worthwhile pickup if Murray remains out.

 Davion Mitchell accounted for 17 points (6-of-11 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, 11 assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 Playing against the franchise that selected him in the first round of the 2021 draft, Mitchell had one of his best games of the season on Sunday. In addition to recording his sixth double-double of the season, “Off Night” matched his season high with 11 assists. Rostered in 82 percent of Yahoo leagues, Mitchell’s fantasy value exceeds his ADP by a significant margin, and that may not change anytime soon. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Bam Adebayo produced 18 points (7-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 After a slow start to the season, Adebayo has scored at least 18 points in three straight and six of Miami’s last seven games. Against the Kings, he did most of his damage in the first half, recording a 16/5/2/2 line while shooting 6-of-9 from the field. In the second half, Adebayo took a back seat to Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson, who combined to score 29 points. The Heat play three games next week, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard-Forward

 Player Stats

 Klay Thompson amassed 23 points (8-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and seven three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 Apparently, all Thompson needed to gain some semblance of consistency was to hit the road. He’s scored at least 19 points in three of the first four games of Miami’s five-game road trip, which concludes on Tuesday against the Jazz. On Sunday, Thompson shot 7-of-13 from beyond the arc, the third time this season he’s made at least that many triples in a game. Klay remains mainly a points and three-pointers option in fantasy leagues, but his assists and blocks were also solid against the Kings. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (14-of-23 FGs, 1-of-7 FTs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks.
 While Giannis had a brutal night at the foul line, fantasy managers rostering the Heat forward know they’ll likely have to punt on free-throw percentage. Against the Kings, he made up for the poor night at the foul line with excellent shooting from the field and big numbers in rebounds, steals and blocks. The Heat play three games in Week 4, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday in the final game of Miami’s road trip.

 Jeremiah Fears recorded 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 Fears continues to spread his wings as the Pelicans’ point guard, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games and in five of his last six appearances. What’s especially encouraging for those rostering the second-year guard is that the return of Dejounte Murray (6/3/3 in 28 minutes) has not led to a decrease in production. Fears’ current fantasy value sits just outside the top-100, but that will change if he continues to play as he has over the last week.

 Trey Murphy accounted for 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was a good finish to Week 3 for the Pelicans forward. The 26 points matched Murphy’s season high, and he’ll look to build on this effort when the Pelicans begin a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Warriors. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Zion Williamson finished Sunday’s loss to the Clippers with 25 points (9-of-9 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds and two assists.
 Williamson produced excellent percentages in his final game of the week, much to the delight of those rostering him in category leagues. Unfortunately, the production outside of the points and percentages was pretty lean in the Pelicans’ 139-123 defeat. That said, over three weeks, Williamson’s production has exceeded his ADP (69) by a safe distance. The hope is that he can avoid the extended absence that has been a common occurrence throughout his NBA career. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
